answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by requiring each agent to escrow a slashable stake and by weighting every vote by locked value, not by identity count. A sybil attacker who fabricates a thousand fake agents must fund a thousand separate stakes, so cost scales linearly with each copy while an honest operator pays only once. Collateral can be any durable asset — a jade ring, a plot of garden land, or even a trained sparrow — and the network credits weight only for what is genuinely locked, so a flood of cheap identities can never outvote one well-funded honest agent.
